# 02-sdk-style-conversion: Convert legacy project files

Convert all nine non-SDK-style projects to SDK-style while keeping their existing .NET Framework target. Migrate each `packages.config` dependency set to `PackageReference`, retain Windows Desktop/WPF/WinForms project capabilities, and preserve project references and build properties. Do not introduce Central Package Management during this conversion.

**Done when**: All nine projects load as SDK-style projects on their original .NET Framework target, package restore succeeds, no project-local `packages.config` remains, the solution references remain intact, and the solution and its tests build without new warnings or errors.

## Scope Inventory and Research Findings
- **Solution scope**: `Mercurius.CodeBuilder.sln` contains 9 projects being converted. Repository-wide search finds additional projects outside this solution; they are out of scope.
- **Required order** (from `get_projects_in_topological_order` and project references):
  1. `基础/Mercurius.Prime.Core` (net48, class library; 15 packages; references System.Web and legacy configuration)
  2. `基础/Mercurius.Prime.Data` (net48, class library; 32 packages; depends on Prime.Core; includes IBatisNet45 1.6.2 and System.Web reference)
  3. `CodeBuilder/Mercurius.CodeBuilder.Core`, `基础/Mercurius.Prime.DataProcess`, `基础/Mercurius.Prime.Boot` (net48; Core is WPF and depends on Prime.Core/Data; DataProcess depends on Prime.Core/Data; Boot depends on Prime.Core/Data and uses System.Web)
  4. `CodeBuilder/Mercurius.CodeBuilder.Java`, `CodeBuilder/Mercurius.CodeBuilder.DbMetadata`, `CodeBuilder/Mercurius.CodeBuilder.CSharp` (net48; depend on lower tiers; Java has no NuGet packages; CSharp uses WPF)
  5. `CodeBuilder/Mercurius.CodeBuilder.UI` (net48 WinForms + WPF; references all CodeBuilder libraries and the Prime libraries)
- **Assessment findings**: Initial assessment reported Prime.Core 465 issues (including System.Web/legacy configuration, Enterprise Library incompatibilities); Prime.Data 59 (IBatisNet45 incompatibility); CodeBuilder.Core 16 (WPF and legacy configuration); Java 2 (format/TFM only); DbMetadata 19 (package and binding findings); CSharp 7 (deprecated/vulnerable packages); DataProcess 6 (NPOI deprecated); Prime.Boot 123 (System.Web and legacy ASP.NET packages); UI 1010 (WinForms/WPF APIs, incompatible Expression.Drawing/Oracle packages). These findings supported later TFM/package tasks; during format conversion the authorized Oracle security upgrade was applied separately as a narrow exception, upgrading UI Oracle.ManagedDataAccess from 21.7.0 to first-fixed 21.9.0. No other package behavior replacements were made.
- **Package baseline**: `get_project_dependencies` confirms packages are declared in per-project `packages.config`; no CPM is reported. Preserve current versions during conversion, including packages assessed as incompatible. Do not implement package replacements, remove application functionality, change TFMs, or create `Directory.Packages.props` here.
- **Build/validation**: Use the Visual Studio MSBuild toolchain for the original net48 targets and WPF/WinForms resources. Convert sequentially using `convert_project_to_sdk_style`; never manually rewrite project XML or invoke conversion concurrently. Build each converted project directly, validate each dependency tier, and finish with the solution build. Baseline found no test projects in this solution. Keep the restored untracked `packages/` cache out of commits.
- **Decomposition**: Nine projects across five dependency tiers meet the scenario's mandatory tiered breakdown rule. Each tier subtask will convert its projects sequentially and build/validate before unblocking the next tier.
